title: Day 518 and still the best, simplest tool for ADHD support
body:
Need I say more? I love this app. I’ve tried many, and this is the only one that’s stayed the course. We all have our preferences, different mashups of neurodivergent traits, usually with a few other bits and bobs thrown in to keep it spicy. But Numo is by far the best one for my individual characteristics and personality. I enjoy the little dopamine shots when I see my daily streak, earn new colours, sounds, etc. 
The best part is ticking my to-do list. I don’t always tick everything, but it lets me see what I’ve done and haven’t done. I’ve learnt I do more than I think - or remember - I have and that’s a little boost in itself. I can remind myself if things i need to do in the near or distant future and I don’t have to think about it. Much better than my phone calendar which I often miss (it’s too dreary, boring, and makes me feel anxious) and alarms often don’t play! Numo is a nice place to wake up to and see what’s in store - everything from brushing my teeth (right ADHDers?) to friends birthdays and paying bills. Daily, weekly, monthly, one-off or pretty much any combination. 
Finally, any problems with it have been quickly dealt with by the Numo team.
I fully expect ti write a similar one in another 518 days - especially if I add a task in Numo!! Thank you for creating it ☺️🙏⚡️❤️

title: 5 stars, but the social side still needs work
body:
I honestly didn’t see myself using this app for any real length of time, but it’s turned out to be my favourite place to manage those random to-do items I’m constantly forgetting - like what day the bins go out, or that I need to teach myself how to remove a hard drive so I can bin an old desktop. 

I like that reminders can be entered as one-offs or repeating habits. I like the option to share tasks I complete publicly, or not. 

I would love it if they had a way you could combine multiple tasks into an overall task, with the original tasks as subtasks - sometimes I don’t realise tasks are linked until I’m several in, and copying those manually is bleh.

I don’t fully understand the social stuff, but I appreciate that the developers are trying new things out. Just give us a forum style place where we can raise topics and ask (and search) for questions and answers people have shared. Keep the global social feed (the ability to like and reply), but give us a “friends” feed and let us connect with people we want to see in it.

Also, as great as this app is I really struggle to see myself paying the £9.99 a month subscription. £4.99? Hell yes. But this shouldn’t cost more than paramount+. 

Those are the most constructive thoughts I could share, but this really is a useful and weirdly, wonderfully rewarding way to keep me in touch with my daily and random to-do’s!

author: createdshots

title: Irritating and counterproductive
body:
Despite the annoying cartoon nonsense, I tried using this app. 

I’m working on my Macbook mid-morning when my iPhone lights up. “Hey! Got a few minutes for a procrastination story!?”

No! NO!! I have not. I’m doing my work!!! 

You’re supposed to HELP me focus. Not distract me yourself!!!!

You … you … yes. I’m going to say it. Unlike any ADHDer, Numo App:

YOU HAD ONE JOB!!!!!!!!!

As for that cartoon nonsense …

“Cringe-free”? More like cringe-ful. 

This app purports to be for all ages but looks more aimed at 14yos than 40yos. Maybe I’m not the target market. 

I don’t want a “non-serious” username like, say, HyperfocusHound or ADDicted2Luv. ADHD can be a superpower as well as a curse but I’ve had quite enough of it being a hideous curse. 

Staying focused at work so I don’t get fired isn’t funny or cute. It’s life or death. The grinning strawberry doesn’t make me feel better. Instead, it lowers my opinion of the developers so rapidly there’s a sonic boom.

author: j_crai

title: Fake Reviews & High Subscription Fees
body:
On the surface this is a great idea and could be an amazing app. The premise of it is simple, easy to set up and fun, however, I agree with a lot of the genuine reviews on here that the execution is pretty basic and lacking a lot of functionality. 

The UI is nice and clean but the UX is poor and as a person with ADHD I find it mildly frustrating to use at times which is the opposite of what you want.

eg. You can't reorder your todo list or set priorities so everything is out of order, meaning you have to search your to do list for what you have to do or before you type it out in the morning you've got to plan your day out completely then type in order = Not so great for people with ADHD.

The tools are a nice touch but after you complete things like the emotion map, they disappear off into the ether to be immediately forgotten about...and the tone of voice used in the app can be pretty condescending at times.

This app has a long loooooong way to go but given they charge over £15/month, it's not worth the pain and the developer response essentially saying 'ADHD coaching is $200 so we're doing you a favour' is pretty shocking.

There are far more developed apps designed for ADHD that also aren't perfect but cost around £25/year and clearly put a lot more focus into the user experience.

Test your app better.
author: nicolaanne11

title: App is mediocre but has big potential
body:
The concept of the app seems very appealing but it just hasn’t been executed very well. The list function is okay but you can’t reorder tasks to prioritise what you need to get done first (incase you burn out midway through getting things done). It also glitches sometimes when you try to add the task to your task page. It’s like a glorified version of the Apple List app but with less flexibility. The ‘hacks’ are kind of patronising, example: “If it takes less than 5 minutes to do the task, just do it immediately”???? 

I do however like the ‘Squad’ page where people can interact with your tasks. Only problem is that you don’t get a notification or a page that collates your reactions to keep you motivated. It just comes up on the squad page if you catch it at the right time alongside with everyone else’s random tasks. 

The ‘Learn’ page is nice but I never really get around to using it. I have to end one course to be able to start a new one which means I don’t get to read the new topic I’ve become interested in and I don’t look at the current topic because it temporarily does not interest me. I cannot commit to going through a whole story and doing all of their inbuilt tasks in one go.

If it had a similar layout to Instagram I think it would actually work really well.  A ‘Learn’ page being similar to the Explore page to pick up quick tips and tricks, a notification centre showing you all the people congratulating you on finishing tasks (for a lil dopamine hit) and your home page showing everyone else doing their tasks.

I do understand that this app is in its early stages of development and I have high hopes for the future but I will probably go back to writing lists in my notepad.
